Qubit islands and their Josephson junctions. Choose one by the qubit style you want to place.

## `disk_flip_chip_qubit`

A two-die flip-chip transmon site: a disk island joined to ground by one Manhattan junction, with four optional arc claws. The readout and drive lines sit on the control die.

![Default layout of `disk_flip_chip_qubit`.](../../_static/images/components/disk_flip_chip_qubit_layers.svg)

Details: [Component guide](../../public-pdk-examples/components/disk_flip_chip_qubit.qmd)

## `kosen2024_flip_chip_xmon_qubit`

A public-preview four-port flip-chip Xmon coupling topology: crossed bars and four qubit-coupling electrodes on the qubit chip, with one Manhattan junction by default. XY drive and readout geometry belong to the facing chip and are not included.

![Default layout of `kosen2024_flip_chip_xmon_qubit`.](../../_static/images/components/kosen2024_flip_chip_xmon_qubit.svg)

Details: [Function reference](../../reference/cells.kosen2024_flip_chip_xmon_qubit.qmd)

## `manhattan_style_junction`

A Manhattan junction: the overlap cross that is fabricated, plus a straight sheet that stands in for the junction as a lumped port in FEM simulation. The image shows the fabricated cross.

![Default layout of `manhattan_style_junction`.](../../_static/images/components/manhattan_style_junction.svg)

Details: [Function reference](../../reference/cells.manhattan_style_junction.qmd)
